title: Activity Experience — the M0 gate, read at its DECIDED first round
note: The M0 gate with a SECOND round, opened at its first (spec §7.2 R1: a non-latest revision is read-only). The story is the one the spec names: the first M0 approval bound a plan, the Architecture was then amended, the plan went stale and was recomputed, and round 2 is awaiting the human again. Round 1 is therefore a decided, persisted round — a subject, a roster, a human verdict and a resolved thread — and the route opens it, so the screen must render the read-only history: the banner and Back to latest, this round's verdicts and thread, the CURRENT artifact under the history caption, NO submit bar, no stale surface (the sdpReview slot is stale in this capture, and a past round is not where it is reconciled), and no focusable option card. Same summary project-view capture as project-design-m0.json, byte for byte. Task 12 corrected the round's one anchor: sdpOptionAnchor takes the option's SOLUTION KIND (`compressedSolution`), and the fixture carried `compressed`, which matches no option row — so the card could only fall into the margin's UNPLACED group, and §7.5 gap 1 (CommentableList's ReadOnlyRow enrols every row of a READ-ONLY surface, so a past round's thread still sits level with what it was about) was proved nowhere. Task 12 gave the round a SECOND comment, anchored to an activity-list row (`$.activities[name="C-review-engine"]`). That is the anchor CommentableList's ReadOnlyRow enrols on the M0 body's ActivityListView, so the card sits LEVEL with the row it is about even though the whole surface is read-only — §7.5 gap 1, which nothing else in the fixture set could prove. The FINAL FIX WAVE closed that hole (I4): SdpReviewView's option rows now enrol `sdpOptionAnchor(solutionKind)` through an extracted `OptionRow`, exactly as ContractSignatureList's OpRow does, so the first comment (`m0r1c1`, on `compressedSolution`) is PLACED too and this fixture proves BOTH enrolments. The control moved to a THIRD comment, `m0r1c3`, anchored to `$.options[kind=hybridSolution]` — an option The Method never assembles, so no row can ever enrol it. That card is unplaceable by construction, not by omission, and it is what keeps the placement assertions a discrimination rather than a tautology.

verdicts.summary: Normal it is. The compressed option buys five weeks for a third more cost and I do not need the five weeks.

thread.text: Compression at 28% with no death-zone activity — why is normal still the recommendation?

replies.text: Because the compressed network has two 0-float chains and no float left to absorb a single slip; normal keeps 11 days.

thread.text: C-ReviewEngine at 15 days is the longest single activity on the critical path. Is that the estimate, or the contract it has to satisfy?

replies.text: The estimate. Its contract is five ops; the 15 days are the routing table and the policy floor, both of which the standard check reads.

thread.text: The hybrid option we discussed is not in the table. Was it excluded, or never assembled?

replies.text: Never assembled: The Method's four options are the whole set, and a fifth would have no risk curve to sit on.
